En cas de groupement conjoint, le mandataire sera solidaire, pour l'exécution du marché public, de chacun des membres du groupement, pour ses obligations contractuelles à l'égard de l’acheteur. references_experience.text: énements : 2 formats de kakémonos (80x200 cm) pour les événements du projet (conférences, salons, ateliers). quelques éléments graphiques génériques permettant de décliner l’identité sur les supports de communication du projet. Supports pédagogiques illustrés destinés aux enseignants : conception d'une série de supports visuels (affiches, posters pédagogiques) présentant de manière ludique et accessible le projet EARTH-LIFE (primaire, collège, lycée). The Sizing Technology Pilot is a direct extension of this modernization mandate, seeking to apply advanced digital, computer vision, and AI-driven measurement extraction capabilities to a fundamental logistical process: Soldier and Cadet outfitting. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate issue experience. The scope of this requirement encompasses both body and foot scanning to modernize the issuance of both uniforms and footwear. The scope covers four primary initial accession pipelines: (1) Initial Entry Training (IET) Soldiers processing through Military Entrance Processing Stations (MEPS); (2) United States Military Academy (West Point) Cadets; (3) contracted Senior Reserve Officers' Training Co

forms_signatures.text: ment of the Army (HQDA) G-4 Logistics Initiatives Group is the directorate responsible for leading the Army’s digital transformation in logistics and Installation, Energy, and Environment (IE&E). The G-4 drives policy, governance, investment strategy, and the technical integration of logistics automated information management systems. Their strategic focus centers on logistics modernization through integrated information systems, scaling artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) analytics, and improving supply chain reliability across Army operations. The Sizing Technology Pilot is a direct extension of this modernization mandate, seeking to apply advanced digital, computer vision, and AI-driven measurement extraction capabilities to a fundamental logistical process: Soldier and Cadet outfitting. The Army is exploring a Sizing Technology Pilot to modernize the Soldier and Cadet outfitting process by using body scanning, foot scanning, computer vision, and/or AI- driven measurement extraction to generate accurate measurements and translate them into recommended uniform and footwear sizing. This capability is intended to support personnel earlier in the accessions pipeline than is possible today, in support of a faster, more consistent, and more accurate iss

l, non- contact methods and translating those measurements into recommended standard Army uniform and footwear sizes. Accurate measurement-to-size mapping — not a 3D visual try-on or avatar rendering, is the core capability sought. The Army is seeking a solution that will operate reliably across a wide spectrum of Army operating environments, minimize the training burden on Soldiers and administering staff, and be capable of integrating with designated Army data systems to support downstream sizing and issue processes. 3. REQUIRED AND DESIRED SOLUTION ATTRIBUTES. Required Attributes: The proposed solution shall meet the following mandatory requirements: • Comprehensive Scanning and Environmental Resilience: Must capture both body and foot measurements sufficient to determine standard Army uniform and footwear sizing using automated, digital, non-contact methods that eliminate manual measurements. The capture hardware must be transportable and capable of operating reliably across a wide spectrum of environments, including indoor facilities and austere outdoor settings, accommodating real-world conditions such as variable ambient lighting and physical space constraints. • Data Translation & Mapping: Must translate captured body and foot measurements into recommen

tive, requiring minimal training for both the Soldiers and Cadets being measured and the administering staff. • Security & Compliance: Must comply with all applicable DoD Risk Management Framework (RMF) requirements and be capable of obtaining the appropriate Authorization to Operate (ATO) prior to processing any Soldier and Cadet data (all captured data must be encrypted at rest and in transit). Impact Level 5 (IL5) is required prior to full-scale enterprise deployment. Pilot execution will be conducted in an isolated, test/dummy network environment. • Data Management & Privacy: Must support a defined data retention and deletion schedule that strictly adheres to Army records-management and Privacy Act requirements. • Inclusive Accuracy: Must produce accurate measurements across the complete spectrum of body types, statures, and physical compositions represented in the Army accession and training population. • Accessibility (Section 508): Must provide an accessible alternative process for Soldiers and Cadets who are unable to use, or elect not to use, the scanning solution; any user-facing digital interface must strictly comply with Section 508 accessibility standards. • Data Ownership & Licensing: Must allow the Government to retain exclusive ownership of all Soldier and Cadet sizing data as well as any vendor-generated technical or derived data. • Hardware Agility & Openness: The proposed solution must be hardware- agnostic to the greatest extent possible, avoiding dependency on proprietary, single-source capture devices. The software application must be capable of evolving to support new generations of commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) devices. The physical hardware proposed for the pilot must be agile, deployable, and suitable for the respective operating environments

insurance_bonds.text: EMENT OF OBJECTIVES (SOO) For Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) Topic Area 3 1.0 Purpose The objective of this effort is to address cyber threats to national critical space missions (e.g., Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT), Missile Warning/Missile Tracking (MW/MT), Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR), and Satellite Communications (SATCOM)) through the research, design, development, testing, and demonstration of a comprehensive Secure by-Design Space Vehicle (SDSV) system. 2.0 Background Space vehicles are increasingly recognized as vulnerable platforms facing sophisticated cyber threats. To ensure mission assurance, there is a critical need to provide advanced defensive solutions for space assets. This project aims to reduce the attack surfaces of space vehicles and implement robust resiliency mechanisms that enable self-protection and rapid recovery from cyber anomalies, leveraging Cyber-Hardened Satellite Software (CHSS) technology. 3.0 Period and Place of Performance • Period of Performance: The anticipated period of performance is a 12-month Base effort, followed by three (3) 12-month Option periods, plus 3 months for final reporting (Total 51 Months). • Place of Performance: The work will be performed primarily at the contractors facilit

When preparing a competitive quotation, vendors should take into consideration benefits provided through the national healthcare system. Quotations should refrain from over customization, and should be “off the shelf”, “commercially available”, or “market ready” products which are designed to be complementary and supplement to the national system in Portugal. The benefit levels listed from section C.1.1 through C.1.24 are a standard package that must be provided. C.1.1 Eligibility: To be eligible to participate in the medical plan, LE Staff (both full time and part time) must be: -- Paid under the terms of the Local Compensation Plan (LCP); and – -- Under a non-temporary direct hire appointment, personal services agreement (PSA), or personal services contract (PSC); or -- Under a temporary direct hire appointment or PSA Fixed Term of one year or more. Not eligible are those working under temporary appointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor l

ointments; those working under a PSC or PSA that is time limited to less than one year; non-personal services contract personnel and their employees, supplied by an independent contractor licensed to do business in Portugal who provides services to other local RFP 19GE5026Q0035 – LES Health Insurance Services for U.S. Embassy Lisbon Page 6 of 21 organizations as well as to the U.S. Mission; employees working on an intermittent or When Actually Employed (WAE) schedule; Peace Corps personal services contractors and Recreation Association employees. C.1.2 Riders: There are no riders under this contract. C.1.3 Periods of Ineligibility: Employees and their dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment for which premiums are not paid. Additionally, employee's dependents are not entitled to health benefits during any period of employment during which the employee was not eligible to participate. During a period of extended Leave Without Pay (LWOP) or other unpaid leave beyond one pay period, the employee is responsible for the full cost of the insurance premiums for self and dependents. The Mission will pay the premiums directly to the Contractor and will collect the full cost from the employee on a quarterly basis. Alternatively
